name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood for my interior trim?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood for my interior trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing between MDF (medium-density fiberboard) and solid wood depends on your budget, environment, and whether you plan to paint or stain. MDF is smooth, uniform, budget-friendly, and ideal for painted baseboards or crown molding in climate-controlled living areas. However, MDF swells if exposed to standing water, making solid wood or moisture-resistant materials a safer bet in bathrooms. If you want natural grain, stained trim, or durable baseboards that withstand heavy impacts in busy hallways, solid lumber like pine, poplar, or oak is the better investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: MDF is cost-effective and paint-ready for dry living areas, while solid wood offers superior impact resistance, moisture tolerance, and options for wood staining.
